{{< pagebreak >}}

## Background

Hospital-acquired (nosocomial) infections are rarely observed in their entirety. A patient may be infected days before a diagnostic test returns positive, and patients who are discharged or never tested remain invisible to standard surveillance. The result is a fragmented picture of the outbreak: a subset of cases is detected, each recorded with a positive-test date rather than the true infection date, and the underlying transmission links are completely latent.

This supplement documents three use cases of the simulation and inference framework:

1.  **Simulating** a synthetic outbreak on a two-ward hospital and inspecting its dynamics against the deterministic SIS endemic equilibrium.
2.  **Reconstructing** the posterior distribution over transmission trees from the incomplete observed data via Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC).
3.  **Assessing the value of genomic data** by comparing reconstruction accuracy with and without pairwise SNP distances.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## The Model {#sec-model}

### Hospital structure

The hospital is modelled as a three-level spatial hierarchy: beds are nested inside rooms, rooms inside wards. All experiments below use a two-ward layout:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-layout
#| tbl-cap: "Hospital layout used in all experiments."
data.frame(
  Level = c("Wards", "Rooms per ward", "Beds per room", "Total beds"),
  Value = c(
    length(unique(Positions$Ward)),
    NumRooms / length(unique(Positions$Ward)),
    NumBeds / NumRooms,
    NumBeds
  )
) |>
  kable(booktabs = TRUE, col.names = c("Level", "Count"), align = "lr")
```

### Transmission dynamics

Each day, a susceptible bed $i$ is exposed to the infectious pressure from every currently infected bed $j$. The per-contact transmission rate depends on the spatial relationship between $i$ and $j$:

$$\beta_{ij} =
\begin{cases}
\beta_{\text{room}} & \text{if } i \text{ and } j \text{ share a room} \\[4pt]
\beta_{\text{ward}} & \text{if } i \text{ and } j \text{ share a ward (different rooms)} \\[4pt]
\beta_{\text{hosp}} & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}$$

with default values $\beta_{\text{room}} = 0.08$, $\beta_{\text{ward}} = 0.005$, $\beta_{\text{hosp}} = 0.0005$.

The probability that susceptible bed $i$ **escapes** infection on day $t$ is the product of escape probabilities over all currently infected contacts:

$$P\!\left(\text{escape}_{i} \mid t\right)
= \prod_{j \in \mathcal{I}(t)} \left(1 - \beta_{ij}\right)$$

so the infection probability is $1 - P(\text{escape}_i \mid t)$.

### Basic reproduction number

With $n_s$ potential contacts at spatial scale $s$ and daily discharge rate $p_{\text{dis}}$, the basic reproduction number of the SIS model is

$$\mathcal{R}_0
= \frac{\displaystyle\sum_{s} \beta_s\, n_s}{p_{\text{dis}}}
= \frac{\beta_{\text{room}}\,(n_{\text{room}}-1)
       + \beta_{\text{ward}}\,(n_{\text{ward}}-n_{\text{room}})
       + \beta_{\text{hosp}}\,(N-n_{\text{ward}})}
       {p_{\text{dis}}}$$

For the default parameters, $\mathcal{R}_0 = `r round(R0_val, 2)`$, implying a deterministic SIS endemic prevalence of $1 - 1/\mathcal{R}_0 \approx `r round(100*(1 - 1/R0_val))`\%$.

### Genomic observations

Mutations accumulate along each transmission edge as independent Poisson events with mean $\mu$ per generation. For two cases $i$ and $j$ separated by $\kappa_{ij}$ transmission steps, the observed pairwise SNP distance satisfies

$$D_{ij} \;\sim\; \operatorname{Poisson}\!\left(\mu\,\kappa_{ij}\right)$$

with $\mu = 2$ mutations per transmission event.

### Bayesian reconstruction

Let $\mathbf{a}$ denote the vector of ancestor assignments (with $a_i = \text{NA}$ indicating community importation) and $\mathbf{t}_{\text{inf}}$ the vector of infection times. Given observed positive-test records $\mathbf{t}_{\text{obs}}$ and pairwise SNP distances $\mathbf{D}$, the MCMC targets the joint posterior

$$\pi\!\left(\mathbf{a},\,\mathbf{t}_{\text{inf}}
    \;\middle|\;
    \mathbf{D},\,\mathbf{t}_{\text{obs}}\right)
\;\propto\;
\underbrace{\prod_{i,j} \mathcal{L}(D_{ij} \mid \kappa_{ij})}_{\text{genomic likelihood}}
\;\cdot\;
\underbrace{\prod_i \mathcal{L}(t_{\text{obs},i} \mid t_{\text{inf},i})}_{\text{testing likelihood}}
\;\cdot\;
\underbrace{p_{\text{contact}}(\mathbf{a} \mid \mathbf{t}_{\text{inf}})}_{\text{spatial prior}}
\;\cdot\;
\underbrace{\pi_{\text{import}}(\mathbf{a})}_{\text{import prior}}$$

The spatial prior $p_{\text{contact}}$ assigns higher prior probability to ancestor--descendant pairs that share the same room or ward and whose inferred infection times are temporally consistent with the daily contact matrix.

The sampler alternates four proposal types:

- **Infection time updates** --- each case's infection time is resampled from its conditional given the current ancestor and descendant times.
- **Ancestor updates** --- each case's ancestor is resampled from the conditional posterior over all temporally eligible candidates.
- **Subtree shifts** --- a randomly chosen subtree has all infection times shifted simultaneously, improving mixing over correlated times.
- $\kappa$ updates --- the transmission-step parameter is updated jointly for each ancestor--descendant pair.

## Use Case 1 --- Simulating an Outbreak {#sec-sim}

### Setup

```{r}
#| label: sim-run
theta_demo <- local({
  th        <- theta
  th$P$Init <- c(1, rep(0, NumBeds - 1), rep(0, NumRooms))
  th
})

set.seed(81369)
outbreak <- simulate_outbreak(45, theta_demo)
```

A single infected patient is seeded in bed 1 on day 0 and the model is run for 45 days. This yielded `r nrow(outbreak$CaseRec)` total infections, of which `r nrow(outbreak$ObsRec)` were detected (tested positive before discharge). Only cases that test positive *before* discharge enter the observed data set; the remaining `r nrow(outbreak$CaseRec) - nrow(outbreak$ObsRec)` infected patients form the **hidden** portion of the outbreak.

### Prevalence dynamics

```{r}
#| label: fig-prevalence
#| fig-cap: "Simulated daily prevalence (blue line) for a 45-day outbreak. The dashed red line is the deterministic SIS endemic equilibrium $1 - 1/\\mathcal{R}_0$; the dotted green line is the simulation-mean prevalence."
#| fig-height: 3.8
prev <- outbreak_prevalence(outbreak)
plot_prevalence(prev)
```

### Ground-truth transmission trees

Each horizontal bar below is a patient stay; directed edges follow the true transmission tree. Edge colour encodes spatial scale (same room, same ward, hospital-wide).

```{r}
#| label: fig-true-tree
#| fig-cap: "Ground-truth transmission tree --- all cases, including unobserved. Edges are coloured by spatial scale of transmission."
#| fig-pos: H
#| out-width: "100%"
if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
  plot_timeline(outbreak, observed = FALSE, show_all_stays = TRUE)
} else {
  p_all <- plot_timeline(outbreak, observed = FALSE, show_all_stays = TRUE)
  save_timeline(p_all, file.path(fig_dir, "true-tree-all.png"), width = 1400)
  knitr::include_graphics(file.path(fig_dir, "true-tree-all.png"))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-obs-tree
#| fig-cap: "Ground-truth tree restricted to observed (test-positive) cases."
#| fig-pos: H
#| out-width: "100%"
if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
  plot_timeline(outbreak, observed = TRUE, show_all_stays = TRUE)
} else {
  p_obs <- plot_timeline(outbreak, observed = TRUE, show_all_stays = TRUE)
  save_timeline(p_obs, file.path(fig_dir, "true-tree-obs.png"), width = 1400)
  knitr::include_graphics(file.path(fig_dir, "true-tree-obs.png"))
}
```

## Use Case 2 --- Bayesian Reconstruction via MCMC {#sec-mcmc}

Given only the observed case records and pairwise SNP distances, we run MCMC to reconstruct the posterior distribution over transmission trees.

```{r}
#| label: mcmc-run
set.seed(2413)
fit <- mcmc(outbreak, N_samples = 3000, burn_in = 500)

score <- ancestry_score(
  outbreak$ObsRec$Anc2,
  fit$anc,
  outbreak$ObsRec$Adm,
  outbreak$ObsRec$PTest
)
```

### Reconstruction accuracy

```{r}
#| label: tbl-score
#| tbl-cap: "Ancestry reconstruction accuracy metrics (3 000 post-burn-in samples)."
data.frame(
  Metric = c("Mode accuracy", "Mean $P$(true ancestor)",
             "Mean lift", "Log skill"),
  Value  = round(c(score$mode_accuracy, score$mean_p_true,
                   mean(score$lift),    score$log_skill), 3),
  Description = c(
    "Fraction of cases where the posterior-mode ancestor equals the true ancestor",
    "Average posterior probability assigned to the true ancestor",
    "Mean ratio of $P$(true ancestor) to uniform-random baseline",
    "Mean $\\log$(lift); 0 indicates performance at chance"
  )
) |>
  kable(booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE,
        col.names = c("Metric", "Value", "Description"),
        align = c("l", "r", "l"))
```

### Posterior-mode reconstruction

```{r}
#| label: fig-reconstruction
#| fig-cap: "Posterior-mode reconstruction overlaid on the ground-truth tree. Green edges are correctly inferred transmissions; red edges are errors. Edge width reflects posterior support."
#| fig-pos: H
#| out-width: "100%"
if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
  plot_timeline_mode(outbreak, fit, color_edges = TRUE, color_nodes = FALSE)
} else {
  p_mode <- plot_timeline_mode(outbreak, fit, color_edges = TRUE, color_nodes = FALSE)
  save_timeline(p_mode, file.path(fig_dir, "reconstruction-mode.png"), width = 1400)
  knitr::include_graphics(file.path(fig_dir, "reconstruction-mode.png"))
}
```

### MCMC convergence diagnostics

```{r}
#| label: fig-diagnostics
#| fig-cap: "MCMC convergence panel. Top row: trace and running mean of community imports (left) and mean infection time (right), with orange dashed lines marking the ground truth. Bottom row: ancestry raster (cases $\\times$ iterations; rapid switching indicates good mixing) and per-case posterior entropy coloured by mode correctness."
#| fig-height: 8.5
plot_mcmc_diagnostics(fit, outbreak)
```

### Posterior accuracy per case

```{r}
#| label: fig-mode-vs-truth
#| fig-cap: "Scatter of $P$(true ancestor) vs.\\ posterior-mode probability for each case. Points above the diagonal indicate cases where the mode concentrates on the wrong ancestor. Point size is inversely proportional to the number of eligible ancestors."
#| fig-height: 4.2
plot_mode_vs_truth(fit, outbreak)
```

## Use Case 3 --- Value of Genomic Data {#sec-genetics}

We re-run MCMC on the same outbreak with `use_genetics = FALSE`, replacing the Poisson genomic likelihood with a flat term, to isolate the contribution of SNP distances.

```{r}
#| label: mcmc-nogen
set.seed(8831)
fit_nogen <- mcmc(outbreak, N_samples = 3000, burn_in = 500,
                  use_genetics = FALSE)

score_nogen <- ancestry_score(
  outbreak$ObsRec$Anc2,
  fit_nogen$anc,
  outbreak$ObsRec$Adm,
  outbreak$ObsRec$PTest
)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-compare
#| tbl-cap: "Reconstruction accuracy with and without genomic data."
data.frame(
  Metric  = c("Mode accuracy", "Mean $P$(true ancestor)",
              "Mean lift", "Log skill"),
  With    = round(c(score$mode_accuracy,       score$mean_p_true,
                    mean(score$lift),           score$log_skill), 3),
  Without = round(c(score_nogen$mode_accuracy, score_nogen$mean_p_true,
                    mean(score_nogen$lift),     score_nogen$log_skill), 3)
) |>
  kable(booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE,
        col.names = c("Metric", "With genomics", "Without genomics"),
        align = c("l", "r", "r"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-nogen
#| fig-cap: "Posterior-mode reconstruction without genomic data. Compare with @fig-reconstruction: additional errors appear in cases where multiple plausible ancestor--descendant pairs coexist in the same room."
#| fig-pos: H
#| out-width: "100%"
if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
  plot_timeline_mode(outbreak, fit_nogen, color_edges = TRUE, color_nodes = FALSE)
} else {
  p_nogen <- plot_timeline_mode(outbreak, fit_nogen, color_edges = TRUE, color_nodes = FALSE)
  save_timeline(p_nogen, file.path(fig_dir, "reconstruction-nogen.png"), width = 1400)
  knitr::include_graphics(file.path(fig_dir, "reconstruction-nogen.png"))
}
```

Genomic distances contribute most where several infectious individuals overlap in the same room: the SNP count then disambiguates who infected whom beyond what temporal and spatial constraints alone can resolve.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of simulation and inference experiment."
data.frame(
  Parameter = c(
    "Hospital layout",
    "Simulation duration",
    "$\\mathcal{R}_0$",
    "$\\beta_{\\text{room}}$ / $\\beta_{\\text{ward}}$ / $\\beta_{\\text{hosp}}$",
    "$\\mu$ (mutations per transmission)",
    "Daily testing probability",
    "Daily discharge probability",
    "Total simulated cases",
    "Observed cases",
    "MCMC samples (post burn-in)",
    "Burn-in",
    "Mode accuracy --- with genomics",
    "Mode accuracy --- without genomics"
  ),
  Value = c(
    sprintf("%d wards, %d rooms, %d beds",
            length(unique(Positions$Ward)), NumRooms, NumBeds),
    "45 days",
    sprintf("%.2f", R0_val),
    sprintf("%.3f / %.4f / %.5f",
            theta$beta["BrB"], theta$beta["BwB"], theta$beta["BhB"]),
    as.character(theta$mu),
    sprintf("%.0f%%", theta$P$Test[[1]] * 100),
    sprintf("%.0f%%", theta$P$Dis[[1]]  * 100),
    as.character(nrow(outbreak$CaseRec)),
    as.character(nrow(outbreak$ObsRec)),
    "3 000",
    "500",
    sprintf("%.3f", score$mode_accuracy),
    sprintf("%.3f", score_nogen$mode_accuracy)
  )
) |>
  kable(booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE,
        col.names = c("Parameter", "Value"),
        align = c("l", "l"))
```
